```{r GLM ACCESSORY FUNCTIONS FUNCTION}
# Takes a list of CV.glmnet objects, obtained the coefficients from every single one, then averages them
get_cv_coefs = function(model_list, condense = T, plot = T){
  # Arg1 is just a glmnet model of type multinom
  # Arg2 (default T) determines whether or not the zero beta rows should be
  # removed from the final matrix
  coef_df = NULL
  for (model in model_list){
    betas = coef(model, s='lambda.1se')
    coefs = data.frame(Pair = rownames(betas[[1]]))
    for(num in 1:4){
      coefs = cbind(coefs, betas[[num]][,1])
      colnames(coefs)[num+1] = rownames(as.matrix(betas[num]))
    }
    if(condense == T){
      coefs = filter(coefs, coefs[2]!=0)
    }
    if (is.null(coef_df)){
      coef_df = coefs
    }
    else{
      coef_df = rbind(coef_df, coefs)
    }
  }
  coef_df = coef_df %>% group_by(Pair) %>% summarize_all(mean)

  if (plot == T){
    coef_plot = coef_plot(coef_df)
  }
  return(list("coef_df" = coef_df,
              "coef_plot" = coef_plot))
}


coef_plot = function(coef_df){
  coef_df = coef_df %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, abs)
  coef_plot = coef_df %>% pivot_longer(col = -Pair,
                                       names_to = 'variant') %>%
                          ggplot(aes(x=reorder(Pair, -value), y=value, fill=variant))+
                          geom_bar(position = 'dodge', stat='identity')+
                          labs(
                            title = 'Average (absolute value) lasso coefficients by variant',
                            x = "Pairs",
                            y = 'Coefficient'
                          ) +
                          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) +
                          scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Dark2')
  return(coef_plot)
}


# USED BY THE MULTI_PERFORMANCE_VIZ FUNCTION TO OBTAIN PERFORMANCE METRICS FROM EACH ELEMENT WITHIN THE LIST
# Only compatible with current performance metric output (rows: iteration, accuracy, kappa, delta_F1, omi_F1, wt_F1, beta_F1, average_F1)
extract_performance_metrics = function(list_of_results, ordered_list_of_dabs, object_to_obtain = 'performance_metrics'){
  # Getting averages
  # Getting Kappa and accuracy
  performance_metric_list = sapply(list_of_results, function (x) x[object_to_obtain])
  averages = sapply(performance_metric_list, function (x) x %>% filter(iteration == 'Averages'))
  Accuracy = unlist(averages[row.names(averages) == 'accuracy'])
  Kappa = unlist(averages[row.names(averages) == 'kappa'])
  
  # Produces a list (#dabs * 4 in length) that contains the values in the following arrangement:
  #     dab1_delta, dab1_omi, dab1_wt, dab1_beta, dab2_delta, dab2_omi, dab2_wt dab2_beta, ...
  #     the order is dependent on the rownames ordering in the matrix, NOT the ordering in the list below 
  f1_metrics = c("Delta_F1", "WT_F1", "Omi_F1", "Beta_F1")
  f1s = unlist(averages[rownames(averages) %in% f1_metrics,])

  # This will be the final dataframe that contains all the values
  dabwise_performance = data.frame("dAb" = ordered_list_of_dabs)
  
  # Eventually will cbind this dataframe to the dabwise performance
  temp_f1_df = data.frame(matrix(nrow = 1, ncol = 4))
  colnames(temp_f1_df) = rownames(averages)[rownames(averages) %>% str_detect("F1")] 
  
  # Obtain the first 4 values, these are the associated vals from the matrix corresponding to the first dAb
  for (val in 1:length(ordered_list_of_dabs)){
    start_ind = 1 + length(f1_metrics)*(val-1)
    temp_metrics = f1s[start_ind:(start_ind+4)]
    temp_f1_df = rbind(temp_f1_df, temp_metrics)
  }
  temp_f1_df = na.omit(temp_f1_df)
  temp_perf_metrics = cbind(Accuracy, Kappa, temp_f1_df) %>% signif(digits=3)
  
  dabwise_performance = cbind(dabwise_performance, temp_perf_metrics)

  # Might add standard deviations later but for now Im leaving it out because it's a huge pain in the ass
  return(dabwise_performance)
}


# MULTI_PERFORMANCE_VIZ -> USED TO OBTAIN PERFORMANCE METRICS FROM A LIST OF RESULTS
# THE LIST OF RESULTS SHOULD FOLLOW THE SAME FORM AS THOSE PRODUCED IN GLM_CV FUNCTIONS
# HANDLES PLOTTING BUT CALLS THE EXTRACT_PERFORMANCE_METRICS FUNCTION TO ACTUALLY OBTAIN VALUES TO PLOT
multi_performance_viz = function(list_of_results, ordered_list_of_dabs, object_to_obtain = 'performance_metrics'){
  
  # Obtaining performance metrics
  perf_metrics = extract_performance_metrics(list_of_results, ordered_list_of_dabs, object_to_obtain)
  long_performance_metrics = perf_metrics %>% pivot_longer(cols = -dAb, names_to = 'metric')
  
  # I want bar graphs with grouped cols for each dab and all dabs on a single graph organized by greatest kappa
  col_plot = ggplot(long_performance_metrics, aes(x=dAb, y=value, fill = metric)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge")+
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Dark2')
  print(col_plot)
  
  col_plot_2 = ggplot(long_performance_metrics, aes(x=metric, y=value, fill = metric))+
    geom_bar(stat="identity")+
    geom_text(aes(label=value, y=value, vjust = 2))+
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Dark2', type = "qual")+
    facet_wrap(~dAb)
    
  print(col_plot_2)
  # I want the top N cAbs from each dab
}


# GLM PERFROMANCE FUNCTION
# Used in GLM_FS function to obtain performance metrics based on model predictions
get_glm_performance = function(predictions, y_test){
  if(length(levels(predictions)) == length(levels(y_test))){
    conf_matrix = confusionMatrix(y_test, predictions, mode = 'everything')
    
    Delta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Delta'][[1]]
    Omi_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Omicron'][[1]]
    WT_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: WT'][[1]]
    Beta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Beta'][[1]]
      
    perf_metrics = data.frame("accuracy" = conf_matrix$overall[[1]],
                                  "kappa" = conf_matrix$overall[[2]],
                                  "Delta_F1" = Delta_F1,
                                  "Omi_F1" = Omi_F1,
                                  "WT_F1" = WT_F1,
                                  "Beta_F1" = Beta_F1,
                                  "Average_f1" = mean(c(Delta_F1, Omi_F1, WT_F1, Beta_F1), na.rm = T))
    return(list("perf_metrics" = perf_metrics,
                "conf_matrix" = conf_matrix))
  }
  else{
    reference = y_test
    conf_matrix = CrossTable(predictions,
                             y_test,
                             prop.chisq = F)
    table = conf_matrix$t
    
    # Convert table to df to make it easier to work with
    N = length(reference)
    tab_df = as.data.frame(table) %>% mutate_if(is.factor, as.character)
    
    # Accuracy is the sum of when the x and y are the same divided by the total
    accuracy = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x==tab_df$y]) / N
    
    # kappa is 
    # po is the accuracy of the model
    po = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x==tab_df$y])/sum(tab_df$Freq)
    
    # pe is the agreement between the probabilities of each class based on the reference and the predicted
    true_beta_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$y=='Beta']) / N
    pred_beta_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x=='Beta']) / N 
    
    true_omicron_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$y=='Omicron']) / N 
    pred_omicron_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x=='Omicron']) / N 
    
    true_delta_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$y=='Delta']) / N 
    pred_delta_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x=='Delta']) / N 
    
    true_wt_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$y=='WT']) / N 
    pred_wt_percent = sum(tab_df$Freq[tab_df$x=='WT']) / N 
    
    pe = ((true_beta_percent * pred_beta_percent) / N^2) +
         ((true_omicron_percent * pred_omicron_percent) / N^2) + 
         ((true_delta_percent * pred_delta_percent) / N^2) +
         ((true_wt_percent * pred_wt_percent) / N^2)
    
    kap = (po - pe)/(1 - pe)
    
    perf_metrics = data.frame("accuracy" = accuracy,
                                  "kappa" = kap,
                                  "Delta_F1" = NA,
                                  "Omi_F1" = NA,
                                  "WT_F1" = NA,
                                  "Beta_F1" = NA,
                                  "Average_f1" = NA)
    
    return(list("perf_metrics" = perf_metrics,
                "conf_matrix" = table))
  }
}
```

```{r BASE GLM}
# GLMs with moving thresholds but no feature selection
# most recent change: Shifted scaling from threshold_df assignment to each resampling loop to allow for the inclusion of complex transformations
# namel yeo-johnson
glm_no_fs = function(df, target, k1, num_repeats, threshold, alpha_value){
  perf_df = NULL
  conf_table_list = NULL
  opt_model_list = list()
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
                  select(-c(Conc., Replicates)) %>%
                  mutate_if(is.numeric, scale)
  
  for(rep in 1:num_repeats){
    
    global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
    conf_table_ind = 1+(5*(rep-1))
    
    
    for (fold1 in 1:k1){
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[fold1]],]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[fold1]],]
    
    
      # Create model matrix -- .-1 term removes the intercept 
      model_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
      
      x_global_test_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, global_test)
      y_global_test = global_test[[target]]
      
      x_global_train_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, global_train)
      y_global_train = global_train[[target]]
        
      # Create initial models
      # This creates a set of models trained with varying lambdas. From here, I can obtain the optimal lambda and its associated coefficients.
      # I train this internal loop without an intercept because I don't actually care what it is, nor does it matter if the model is made worse by it.
      # I need relative importances of features and internal rough performance. I train the later global model with an intercept, however
      internal_model = cv.glmnet(x_global_train_matrix, y_global_train, 
                                 family = "multinomial",
                                 alpha = alpha_value,
                                 type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                                 nfolds = 5,
                                 type.measure = 'class',
                                 intercept = F,
                                 parallel = T)
      
      opt_lasso_predict = predict(internal_model, s = internal_model$lambda.1se,
                                  newx = x_global_test_matrix,
                                  type = 'class')
      opt_lasso_predict = as.factor(opt_lasso_predict)
      
      if (length(levels(opt_lasso_predict)) == length(levels(y_global_test))){
        conf_matrix = confusionMatrix(y_global_test, opt_lasso_predict, mode = 'everything')
        # recording performance metrics of each train test split
        Delta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Delta'][[1]]
        Omi_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Omicron'][[1]]
        WT_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: WT'][[1]]
        Beta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Beta'][[1]]
        
        perf_metrics = data.frame("iteration" = conf_table_ind,
                                  "accuracy" = conf_matrix$overall[[1]],
                                  "kappa" = conf_matrix$overall[[2]],
                                  "Delta_F1" = Delta_F1,
                                  "Omi_F1" = Omi_F1,
                                  "WT_F1" = WT_F1,
                                  "Beta_F1" = Beta_F1,
                                  "Average_f1" = mean(c(Delta_F1, Omi_F1, WT_F1, Beta_F1), na.rm = T))
        
        if(is.null(perf_df)){
          perf_df = perf_metrics
        }
        else{
          perf_df = rbind(perf_df, perf_metrics)
        }
        
        # recording actual confusion tables
        table = conf_matrix$table
        conf_table_list[[conf_table_ind]] = table
      }
      
      else{
        print("Basic confusion matrix used:")
        predicted = opt_lasso_predict
        reference = y_global_test
        conf_matrix = CrossTable(predicted,
                                 reference,
                                 prop.chisq = F)
        table = conf_matrix$t
        conf_table_list[[conf_table_ind]] = table
      }
      # Recording optimal models
      opt_model = internal_model
      opt_model_list[[conf_table_ind]] = opt_model
      
      
      
      conf_table_ind = conf_table_ind+1
    }
  }
  # if anyone besides me is seeing this then please don't judge this joke of a fix. I need this array to be numeric, but I also need to pad it by 
  # one value at the start, otherwise, without a value for the iteration column, the values wrap around the df index. I'll never encounter 1000 in normal
  # operation, so it'll never result in a repeat value in the iteration column before it's immediately overwritten
  stdevs = c(1000, sapply(perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  avgs = c(1000, sapply(perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  
  perf_df = rbind(perf_df, avgs = avgs, stdevs = stdevs)
  perf_df$iteration[nrow(perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  perf_df$iteration[nrow(perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  return(list("performance_metrics" = perf_df, 
                  "confusion_matrices" = conf_table_list,
                  "optimal_model_list" = opt_model_list))
}
```

```{r GLM CV WITH FS, warning=FALSE}
# GLMs with moving thresholds AND feature selection 
glm_fs = function(df, target, k1, k2, num_repeats, threshold, alpha_value,
                     n_top_features){
  # I GUARANTEE THAT THE INDEX VAR IS GOING TO BE FUCKED UP AND WILL TAKE ME HOURS TO FIX LMAO
  external_perf_df = NULL
  global_perf_df = NULL
  
  external_conf_table_list = NULL
  global_conf_table_list = NULL
  
  external_opt_model_list = list()
  global_model_list = list()
  
  global_opt_model_list = list()
  average_coef_plot_list = list()
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
                  select(-c(Conc., Replicates)) %>%
                  mutate_if(is.numeric, scale)
  
  for(rep in 1:num_repeats){
  global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
  
  # NEED TO FIX THESE INDEXERS
  # conf_table_ind = 1+(5*(rep-1))
    
  # indices for when I reinstate the num_repeats loop
  global_ind= 1 + (5 * (rep - 1))
  external_ind = 1 + (k1 * k2 * (rep-1))
  
    for (fold1 in 1:k1){
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[fold1]],]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[fold1]],]
    
      external_kfold = createFolds(global_train[[target]], k = k2)
      # external_ind = 1+(5*(fold1-1))
      
      for (fold2 in 1:k2){
        external_train = global_train[-external_kfold[[fold2]],]
        external_test = global_train[external_kfold[[fold2]],]
        
        # Create model matrix -- .-1 term removes the intercept 
        model_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
        
        x_external_test_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_test)
        y_external_test = external_test[[target]]
        
        x_external_train_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_train)
        y_external_train = external_train[[target]]
        
        # Create initial models
        # This creates a set of models trained with varying lambdas. From here, I can obtain the optimal lambda and its associated coefficients.
        # I train this internal loop without an intercept because I don't actually care what it is, nor does it matter if the model is made worse by it.
        # I need relative importances of features and internal rough performance. I train the later global model with an intercept, however
        external_model = cv.glmnet(x_external_train_matrix, y_external_train, 
                                   family = "multinomial",
                                   alpha = alpha_value,
                                   type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                                   nfolds = 5, # nrow(external_train),
                                   type.measure = 'class',
                                   intercept = F,
                                   parallel = T)
        
        opt_lasso_predict = predict(external_model, s = external_model$lambda.1se,
                                  newx = x_external_test_matrix,
                                  type = 'class')
        opt_lasso_predict = as.factor(opt_lasso_predict)
        perf_call = get_glm_performance(opt_lasso_predict, y_external_test)
        external_perf_metrics = cbind(iteration = external_ind, perf_call$perf_metrics)
        external_conf_matrix = perf_call$conf_matrix
        
        if(is.null(external_perf_df)){
          external_perf_df = external_perf_metrics
        }
        else{
          external_perf_df = rbind(external_perf_df, external_perf_metrics)
        }
        external_conf_table_list[[external_ind]] = external_conf_matrix
        external_opt_model_list[[external_ind]] = external_model
        external_ind = external_ind+1
      }
      # Now that the external cv is completed and I have a full list of models, I need
      # to find the average coefficients, then downselect the global training set with them
      coefs_call = get_cv_coefs(external_opt_model_list, plot = T)
      average_coef_plot_list[[global_ind]] = coefs_call$coef_plot
      average_external_coefs = coefs_call$coef_df
      
      average_abs_external_coefs = average_external_coefs %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, abs)
      
      num_features = n_top_features
  
      sorted_coefs = average_abs_external_coefs %>% select_if(is.numeric) %>% 
                      mutate(sum = rowSums(.)) %>% 
                      mutate('Pair' = average_abs_external_coefs$Pair) %>% 
                      arrange(desc(sum))
      
      best_features = sorted_coefs$Pair[1:num_features]
      global_train = cbind(global_train[[target]], global_train[best_features])
      colnames(global_train)[1] = target
      
      global_test = cbind(global_test[[target]], global_test[best_features])
      print("global training data")
      print(global_train)
      colnames(global_test)[1] = target
      
      # Create global model matrices
      global_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
      
      x_global_test_matrix = model.matrix(global_matrix_formula, global_test)
      y_global_test = global_test[[target]]
  
      
      x_global_train_matrix = model.matrix(global_matrix_formula, global_train)
      y_global_train = global_train[[target]]
  
  
      global_model = cv.glmnet(x_global_train_matrix, y_global_train,
                               family = 'multinomial',
                               type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                               type.measure = 'deviance',
                               nfold = 5,
                               parallel = T,
                               alpha = 1,
                               intercept = F)
      
      global_model_list[fold1] = global_model
      
      global_predict = predict(global_model, newx = x_global_test_matrix,
                               type = 'class',
                               s = global_model$lambda.1se)
      
      global_predict = as.factor(global_predict)
      global_perf_call = get_glm_performance(global_predict, y_global_test)
      global_perf_metrics = cbind(iteration = global_ind, global_perf_call$perf_metrics)
      global_conf_matrix = global_perf_call$conf_matrix
      
      if(is.null(global_perf_df)){
        global_perf_df = global_perf_metrics
      }
      
      else{
        global_perf_df = rbind(global_perf_df, global_perf_metrics)
      }
      
      global_conf_table_list[[global_ind]] = global_conf_matrix
      global_opt_model_list[[global_ind]] = global_model
      global_ind = global_ind+1
    
    # Averaging the performance based on the recorded metrics of the external k-fold cv
    # I have this mob deep in the function because I'll eventually have an external number
    # of repeats, and this averaging needs to be when the last repeat concludes
  
    }
  }
  external_stdevs = c(1000, sapply(external_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  external_avgs = c(1000, sapply(external_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  external_perf_df = rbind(external_perf_df, avgs = external_avgs, stdevs = external_stdevs)
  external_perf_df$iteration[nrow(external_perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  external_perf_df$iteration[nrow(external_perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  
  global_stdevs = c(1000, sapply(global_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  global_avgs = c(1000, sapply(global_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  global_perf_df = rbind(global_perf_df, avgs = global_avgs, stdevs = global_stdevs)
  global_perf_df$iteration[nrow(global_perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  global_perf_df$iteration[nrow(global_perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  
  return(list("external_performance_metrics" = external_perf_df, 
                  "external_confusion_matrices" = external_conf_table_list,
                  "external_model_list" = external_opt_model_list,
                  "global_performance_metrics" = global_perf_df,
                  "global_confusion_matrices" = global_conf_table_list,
                  "global_model_list" = global_opt_model_list,
                  "best_features" = sorted_coefs))
}
```

```{r MODEL LOOP, warning=FALSE}
# Builds models and tests performance
model_call_loop = function(df_list, model_type, k1=5, num_repeats=5, threshold=0, alpha_value = 1, k2 = 5, n_top_features = 10){
  # Currently supports model types
  result_list = rep(NULL, length(df_list))
  
  cl = makeCluster(6)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  
  result_ind = 1
  
  if (model_type == "lasso_no_fs"){
    for (df in df_list){
      result_list[[result_ind]] = glm_no_fs(df, "target_vector", k1, num_repeats, threshold = 0, alpha_value = 1)
      result_ind = result_ind + 1
    }
  }
  else if (model_type == "lasso_fs"){
    for(df in df_list){
      print(result_ind)
      result_list[[result_ind]] = glm_fs(df = df,
                                         target = 'target_vector',
                                         k1, k2, num_repeats,
                                         threshold, alpha_value,
                                         n_top_features = n_top_features)
      result_ind = result_ind+1
    }
  }
  stopCluster(cl)
  registerDoSEQ()
  return(result_list)
}
```

```{r FEATURE SELECTION PERFORMANCE BY NUM_FEATURES}
# External resample function (Input is some of the inputs to the master function but also the train test split)
  # - output is a list of external models, external performance
external_resample = function(split_dfs, target = "target_vector", preprocess, num_folds = 5){
  external_perf_df = NULL
  external_perf_temp = NULL
  
  external_model_list = list(1: (length(split_dfs) * num_folds) )
  
  split_index = 1
  for (split in split_dfs){
    external_data = split
    
    external_folds = createFolds(external_data[[target]], k = num_folds)
    
    for (fold in 1:num_folds){
      
      external_train = external_data[-external_folds[[fold]], ]
      external_test = external_data[-external_folds[[fold]], ]
      
      external_preprocess = preProcess(external_train, method = preprocess)
      external_train = predict(external_preprocess, external_train)
      external_test = predict(external_preprocess, external_test)
      
      # Create model matrix -- .-1 term removes the intercept 
      model_matrix_formula = paste(target, "~", ".-1") %>% as.formula()
      
      x_external_test_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_test)
      y_external_test = external_test[[target]]
      
      x_external_train_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_train)
      y_external_train = external_train[[target]]
        
  
      # This creates a set of models trained with varying lambdas. From here, I can obtain the optimal lambda and its associated coefficients.
      # I train this internal loop without an intercept because I don't actually care what it is, nor does it matter if the model is made worse by it.
      # I need relative importances of features and internal rough performance. I train the later global model with an intercept, however
      external_model = cv.glmnet(x_external_train_matrix, y_external_train,
                                 family = "multinomial",
                                 alpha = 1,
                                 type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                                 nfolds = 5,
                                 type.measure = 'class',
                                 intercept = F,
                                 parallel = T)
      
      opt_external_predict = predict(external_model, s = external_model$lambda.1se,
                                     newx = x_external_test_matrix,
                                     type = 'class')
      
      opt_external_predict = as.factor(opt_external_predict)
      external_model_list[[fold + (5 * (split_index - 1)) ]] = external_model
      # Calls get_glm_perfroamcne, which takes in a set of predictions and outputs accuracy, kappa, f1 for each class, and average f1
      # This is necessary because in situations where a model hasnt preidcted any examples of one of the classes, caret confusionMatrix throws an error
      # only a single row of the final df is produced
      get_external_performance = get_glm_performance(opt_external_predict, y_external_test)
      print(get_external_performance$perf_metrics)
      
      
      if(is.null(external_perf_temp)){
        external_perf_temp = get_external_performance$perf_metrics
      }
      
      else{
        external_perf_temp[fold,] = get_external_performance$perf_metrics
      }
    }
    
    
    if(is.null(external_perf_df)){
      external_perf_df = external_perf_temp
    }
    else{
      external_perf_df = rbind(external_perf_df, external_perf_temp)
    }
    
    
    split_index = split_index + 1
  }

  return(list("external_performance" = external_perf_df,
              "external_models" = external_model_list))
}
```

```{r GLM_NO_FS W/ CONCENTRATION COLUMN}
# CONCENTRATION DOES NOT SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACT THE MAJORITY OF MODELS
# I THINK THAT CONC WILL HAVE A BIGGER INFLUENCE ON TREE BASED MODELS
glm_no_fs_conc = function(df, target, k1, num_repeats, threshold, alpha_value){
  perf_df = NULL
  conf_table_list = NULL
  opt_model_list = list()
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
                  select(-c(Replicates)) %>%
                  mutate_if(is.numeric, scale)
  
  for(rep in 1:num_repeats){
    
    global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
    conf_table_ind = 1+(5*(rep-1))
    
    
    for (fold1 in 1:k1){
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[fold1]],]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[fold1]],]
    
    
      # Create model matrix -- .-1 term removes the intercept 
      model_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
      
      x_global_test_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, global_test)
      y_global_test = global_test[[target]]
      
      x_global_train_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, global_train)
      y_global_train = global_train[[target]]
        
      # Create initial models
      # This creates a set of models trained with varying lambdas. From here, I can obtain the optimal lambda and its associated coefficients.
      # I train this internal loop without an intercept because I don't actually care what it is, nor does it matter if the model is made worse by it.
      # I need relative importances of features and internal rough performance. I train the later global model with an intercept, however
      internal_model = cv.glmnet(x_global_train_matrix, y_global_train, 
                                 family = "multinomial",
                                 alpha = alpha_value,
                                 type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                                 nfolds = 5,
                                 type.measure = 'class',
                                 intercept = F,
                                 parallel = T)
      
      opt_lasso_predict = predict(internal_model, s = internal_model$lambda.1se,
                                  newx = x_global_test_matrix,
                                  type = 'class')
      opt_lasso_predict = as.factor(opt_lasso_predict)
      
      if (length(levels(opt_lasso_predict)) == length(levels(y_global_test))){
        conf_matrix = confusionMatrix(y_global_test, opt_lasso_predict, mode = 'everything')
        # recording performance metrics of each train test split
        Delta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Delta'][[1]]
        Omi_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Omicron'][[1]]
        WT_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: WT'][[1]]
        Beta_F1 = conf_matrix$byClass[,'F1']['Class: Beta'][[1]]
        
        perf_metrics = data.frame("iteration" = conf_table_ind,
                                  "accuracy" = conf_matrix$overall[[1]],
                                  "kappa" = conf_matrix$overall[[2]],
                                  "Delta_F1" = Delta_F1,
                                  "Omi_F1" = Omi_F1,
                                  "WT_F1" = WT_F1,
                                  "Beta_F1" = Beta_F1,
                                  "Average_f1" = mean(c(Delta_F1, Omi_F1, WT_F1, Beta_F1), na.rm = T))
        
        if(is.null(perf_df)){
          perf_df = perf_metrics
        }
        else{
          perf_df = rbind(perf_df, perf_metrics)
        }
        
        # recording actual confusion tables
        table = conf_matrix$table
        conf_table_list[[conf_table_ind]] = table
      }
      
      else{
        print("Basic confusion matrix used:")
        predicted = opt_lasso_predict
        reference = y_global_test
        conf_matrix = CrossTable(predicted,
                                 reference,
                                 prop.chisq = F)
        table = conf_matrix$t
        conf_table_list[[conf_table_ind]] = table
      }
      # Recording optimal models
      opt_model = internal_model
      opt_model_list[[conf_table_ind]] = opt_model
      
      
      
      conf_table_ind = conf_table_ind+1
    }
  }
  # if anyone besides me is seeing this then please don't judge this joke of a fix. I need this array to be numeric, but I also need to pad it by 
  # one value at the start, otherwise, without a value for the iteration column, the values wrap around the df index. I'll never encounter 1000 in normal
  # operation, so it'll never result in a repeat value in the iteration column before it's immediately overwritten
  stdevs = c(1000, sapply(perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  avgs = c(1000, sapply(perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  
  perf_df = rbind(perf_df, avgs = avgs, stdevs = stdevs)
  perf_df$iteration[nrow(perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  perf_df$iteration[nrow(perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  return(list("performance_metrics" = perf_df, 
                  "confusion_matrices" = conf_table_list,
                  "optimal_model_list" = opt_model_list))
}
```

```{r GLM CV WITH FS AND BC transform, warning=FALSE}
# ESSENTIALLY A COPY OF GLM_CV_FS WITH JUST THE CHANGELOG BELOW
# GLMs with moving thresholds AND feature selection 
# Changeglog: shifted scaling to the resampling loop
glm_fs_temp = function(df, target, k1, k2, num_repeats, threshold, alpha_value,
                     n_top_features){
  # I GUARANTEE THAT THE INDEX VAR IS GOING TO BE FUCKED UP AND WILL TAKE ME HOURS TO FIX LMAO
  external_perf_df = NULL
  global_perf_df = NULL
  
  external_conf_table_list = NULL
  global_conf_table_list = NULL
  
  external_opt_model_list = list()
  global_model_list = list()
  
  global_opt_model_list = list()
  average_coef_plot_list = list()
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
                  select(-c(Conc., Replicates))
  
  for(rep in 1:num_repeats){
  global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
  
  # NEED TO FIX THESE INDEXERS
  # conf_table_ind = 1+(5*(rep-1))
    
  # indices for when I reinstate the num_repeats loop
  global_ind= 1 + (5 * (rep - 1))
  external_ind = 1 + (k1 * k2 * (rep-1))
  
    for (fold1 in 1:k1){
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[fold1]],]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[fold1]],]
    
      external_kfold = createFolds(global_train[[target]], k = k2)
      # external_ind = 1+(5*(fold1-1))
      
      for (fold2 in 1:k2){
        external_train = global_train[-external_kfold[[fold2]],]
        external_test = global_train[external_kfold[[fold2]],]

        external_preprocess = preProcess(external_train, method = c("scale", "center", "BoxCox"))
        external_train = predict(external_preprocess, external_train)
        external_test = predict(external_preprocess, external_test)
        
        # Create model matrix -- .-1 term removes the intercept 
        model_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
        
        x_external_test_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_test)
        y_external_test = external_test[[target]]
        
        x_external_train_matrix = model.matrix(model_matrix_formula, external_train)
        y_external_train = external_train[[target]]
        
        # Create initial models
        # This creates a set of models trained with varying lambdas. From here, I can obtain the optimal lambda and its associated coefficients.
        # I train this internal loop without an intercept because I don't actually care what it is, nor does it matter if the model is made worse by it.
        # I need relative importances of features and internal rough performance. I train the later global model with an intercept, however
        external_model = cv.glmnet(x_external_train_matrix, y_external_train, 
                                   family = "multinomial",
                                   alpha = alpha_value,
                                   type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                                   nfolds = 5, # nrow(external_train),
                                   type.measure = 'class',
                                   intercept = F,
                                   parallel = T)
        
        opt_lasso_predict = predict(external_model, s = external_model$lambda.1se,
                                  newx = x_external_test_matrix,
                                  type = 'class')
        opt_lasso_predict = as.factor(opt_lasso_predict)
        perf_call = get_glm_performance(opt_lasso_predict, y_external_test)
        external_perf_metrics = cbind(iteration = external_ind, perf_call$perf_metrics)
        external_conf_matrix = perf_call$conf_matrix
        
        if(is.null(external_perf_df)){
          external_perf_df = external_perf_metrics
        }
        else{
          external_perf_df = rbind(external_perf_df, external_perf_metrics)
        }
        external_conf_table_list[[external_ind]] = external_conf_matrix
        external_opt_model_list[[external_ind]] = external_model
        external_ind = external_ind+1
      }
      # Now that the external cv is completed and I have a full list of models, I need
      # to find the average coefficients, then downselect the global training set with them
      coefs_call = get_cv_coefs(external_opt_model_list, plot = T)
      average_coef_plot_list[[global_ind]] = coefs_call$coef_plot
      average_external_coefs = coefs_call$coef_df
      
      average_abs_external_coefs = average_external_coefs %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, abs)
      
      num_features = n_top_features
  
      sorted_coefs = average_abs_external_coefs %>% select_if(is.numeric) %>% 
                      mutate(sum = rowSums(.)) %>% 
                      mutate('Pair' = average_abs_external_coefs$Pair) %>% 
                      arrange(desc(sum))
      
      best_features = sorted_coefs$Pair[1:num_features]
      global_train = cbind(global_train[[target]], global_train[best_features])
      colnames(global_train)[1] = target
      
      global_test = cbind(global_test[[target]], global_test[best_features])
      colnames(global_test)[1] = target
      
      # Create global model matrices
      global_preprocess = preProcess(global_train, method = c("scale", "center", "BoxCox"))
      global_train = predict(global_preprocess, global_train)
      global_test = predict(global_preprocess, global_test)
        
      global_matrix_formula = paste(target, '~', '.-1') %>% as.formula()
      
      x_global_test_matrix = model.matrix(global_matrix_formula, global_test)
      y_global_test = global_test[[target]]
  
      
      x_global_train_matrix = model.matrix(global_matrix_formula, global_train)
      y_global_train = global_train[[target]]
  
  
      global_model = cv.glmnet(x_global_train_matrix, y_global_train,
                               family = 'multinomial',
                               type.multinomial = 'grouped',
                               type.measure = 'deviance',
                               nfold = 5,
                               parallel = T,
                               alpha = 1,
                               intercept = F)
      
      global_model_list[fold1] = global_model
      
      global_predict = predict(global_model, newx = x_global_test_matrix,
                               type = 'class',
                               s = global_model$lambda.1se)
      
      global_predict = as.factor(global_predict)
      global_perf_call = get_glm_performance(global_predict, y_global_test)
      global_perf_metrics = cbind(iteration = global_ind, global_perf_call$perf_metrics)
      global_conf_matrix = global_perf_call$conf_matrix
      
      if(is.null(global_perf_df)){
        global_perf_df = global_perf_metrics
      }
      
      else{
        global_perf_df = rbind(global_perf_df, global_perf_metrics)
      }
      
      global_conf_table_list[[global_ind]] = global_conf_matrix
      global_opt_model_list[[global_ind]] = global_model
      global_ind = global_ind+1
    
    # Averaging the performance based on the recorded metrics of the external k-fold cv
    # I have this mob deep in the function because I'll eventually have an external number
    # of repeats, and this averaging needs to be when the last repeat concludes
  
    }
  }
  external_stdevs = c(1000, sapply(external_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  external_avgs = c(1000, sapply(external_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  external_perf_df = rbind(external_perf_df, avgs = external_avgs, stdevs = external_stdevs)
  external_perf_df$iteration[nrow(external_perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  external_perf_df$iteration[nrow(external_perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  
  global_stdevs = c(1000, sapply(global_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), sd, na.rm = T))
  global_avgs = c(1000, sapply(global_perf_df %>% dplyr::select(-iteration), mean, na.rm = T))
  global_perf_df = rbind(global_perf_df, avgs = global_avgs, stdevs = global_stdevs)
  global_perf_df$iteration[nrow(global_perf_df)-1] = "Averages"
  global_perf_df$iteration[nrow(global_perf_df)] = "Standard_devations"
  
  return(list("external_performance_metrics" = external_perf_df, 
                  "external_confusion_matrices" = external_conf_table_list,
                  "external_model_list" = external_opt_model_list,
                  "global_performance_metrics" = global_perf_df,
                  "global_confusion_matrices" = global_conf_table_list,
                  "global_model_list" = global_opt_model_list,
                  "best_features" = sorted_coefs))
}
```
